|∇θ| measures how fast the loss changes; spectral leverage measures whether the gate can move the quantum state at all." style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;dashed=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingRight=8;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="890" width="1420" height="86" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Why the masks flip — slope vs geometry: θ1 has the largest accumulated |∇| (0.90) → SP keeps it, but its energy lies in null QFIM eigendirections (e1 = 0.12 < τ): the gradient is loud, yet the quantum state barely moves → QFI freezes it. θ2 has a small |∇| (0.20) → SP freezes it, yet e2 = 0.92: it spans the informative eigenspace → QFI keeps it and rescales it by (F_SS + εI)⁻¹.
|∇θ| measures how fast the loss changes; spectral leverage measures whether the gate can move the quantum state at all.
